stories.headline: LangChain raised $300 million Series C led by CapitalG
stories.quote: LangChain, a San Francisco-based provider of AI agent development and management software, raised $300 million in Series C funding. CapitalG led the round and was joined by GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and others.
stories.description: AI agent development and management software

stories.headline: Dreamteam raised $53 million from Accel, Together Fund and Premji Invest
stories.quote: Dreamteam, a Sacramento, Calif.-based provider of AI-native customer relationship management software, raised $53 million from Accel, TogetherFund, and PremjiInvest.

stories.headline: Kindo raised $30 million led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital
stories.quote: Kindo, a Los Angeles-based provider of enterprise AI agent management software, raised $30 million in funding. CrosspointCapital and ForgepointCapital led the round.

stories.headline: Luminal raised $25 million Series A led by Standard Capital
stories.quote: Luminal, a San Francisco-based developer of AI inference compiler software and cloud infrastructure, raised $25 million in Series A funding led by StandardCapital.
stories.description: AI inference compiler software and cloud infrastructure

stories.headline: Accountable raised $20 million in total funding, including a seed round co-led by Acrew Capital and M13
stories.quote: Accountable, a New York City-based consumer tax and civic company cofounded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden, raised $20 million in total funding, including a seed round co-led by AcrewCapital and M13.
stories.stage_as_written: total funding, including a seed round
stories.founder_background: cofounded by Acorns CEO Noah Kerner and Jeff Cruttenden

stories.headline: Rivio raised approximately $15 million Series A extension led by Valor Capital Group
stories.quote: Rivio, a Sao Paulo-based provider of AI-powered hospital management software and services, raised approximately $15 million in a Series A extension. Valor Capital Group led the round and was joined by Monashees.
stories.description: AI-powered hospital management software and services

stories.headline: Athlete To Athlete raised $8 million Series A led by Rally Ventures
stories.quote: Athlete To Athlete, a Santa Monica, Calif.-based provider of virtual mentorship connecting youth athletes with college athletes, raised $8 million in Series A funding. RallyVentures led the round and was joined by NewboundVC, ScrumVentures, and UpHonest Capital.
stories.description: Virtual mentorship connecting youth athletes with college athletes

stories.headline: Sleep.ai raised $5.3 million led by Treasure Coast Ventures
stories.quote: Sleep.ai, a Carlsbad, Calif.-based provider of sleep intelligence software, raised $5.3 million in funding. Treasure Coast Ventures led the round.

stories.headline: Norwest closed its 18th fund at $4 billion
stories.quote: Norwest, a Menlo Park, Calif.-based investment firm, closed its 18th fund at $4 billion to make venture and growth equity investments in technology, health care, and consumer companies across the U.S., India, and Israel.
stories.description: Investment firm making venture and growth equity investments

stories.headline: Tusk Ventures now takes equity for services instead of investing cash, with around 21 startups
stories.quote: Despite a successful run as a conventional VC, which saw Tusk raise $300 million over three funds, he decided to abandon the model in favor of something novel: taking equity in exchange for services rather than cash.
stories.description: Venture firm helping startups navigate regulation

facts.text: The change of model was made in 2025; Tusk had raised $300 million over three funds before it.
facts.quote: In 2025, Tusk made another bold bet. Despite a successful run as a conventional VC, which saw Tusk raise $300 million over three funds, he decided to abandon the model

facts.text: Around 21 startups are on the equity-for-services arrangement.
facts.quote: Tusk says his firm is currently supplying its equity-for-services arrangement to around 21 startups.

facts.text: Fees are $50,000 to $200,000 a month in preferred equity; engagements usually last about 18 months.
facts.quote: “Our fees are between $50,000 and $200,000 a month in preferred equity, scaled to whatever the valuation of the company is. Engagements are usually about 18 months,”

facts.text: The equity is typically paid from the employee pool and is less than 2% of the overall supply.
facts.quote: the equity is typically paid out of a pool set aside for employees, and is less than 2% of the overall supply

facts.text: Tusk's stated target is $20 million to $30 million a year in earned equity over a 10-year period.
facts.quote: “If we can generate, say, $20 million to $30 million a year in earned equity over a 10-year investment period, that’s $200 million to $300 million,” Tusk said.
